newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares edge higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares edge higher on short-covering.

text.p: Short-covering by speculators more than offset selling spurred by an increase in railway freight to nudge Delhi shares to a slightly higher close on Wednesday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 1.24 points higher at 728.26.
Reliance Industries led the charge as speculators made heavy purchases ahead of the budget. Reliance closed 2.50 rupees higher at 266.25. The share had fallen to 259.50 in early trade.

"The higher than expected hike in railway freight of 12 percent proposed in the railway budget triggered some selling but short-covering in some counters attributed to a late recovery in prices," said Manoj Choraria of Choraria Investments.
Railways Minister Ram Vilas Paswan, while presenting the railway budget for 1997/98 (April-March), proposed a 12 percent hike in freight rates but exempted goods like grains, fuel and fertilisers.
He also proposed a 10 percent rise in first class passenger fares in the budget and a 5.0 percent rise in long-distance second class fares.
Industry bodies said the increases would fuel inflation and could hamper economic growth.
TISCO gained 1.50 rupees to 185.40 on domestic institutional buying.
Bajaj Auto closed 6.00 rupees higher at 898.0.

The Delhi Stock Exchange will hold a special post-budget session trading on Friday from 6:00 p.m. (1230 GMT) to 8:00 p.m. (1430 GMT), following the presentation of the government's 1997/98 budget at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT).
The Stock Exchange will also hold a special trading session on Saturday from 9:45 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. (0415-1015 GMT)
